scope: Application/bot retirement repository and credential/runtime service foundation; not a registered API or available UI action.
implemented: One transaction requires actual human owner, matching password/MFA state, active generation-bound session and a live non-administrator bot. Generic platform administration does not substitute for ownership.

Retirement removes bot tokens, memberships, role grants and private state; detaches owner_user_id; strips identity to an immutable tombstone. Shared channel/DM ciphertext and attachment references remain byte-for-byte intact.
Human and bot identity stripping share a transaction helper. Personal assets enter the durable existing cleanup queue; shared attachments are never queued solely because their author is removed.
Legacy/corrupt bots owning servers or child applications are rejected rather than orphaning resources. Retiring an ordinary bot removes its human owner's account-deletion ownership blocker.

Migration 100 rejects new/reassigned tokens for retired, missing or non-bot principals. Token resolution independently rejects retired, non-bot, banned or disabled users even for legacy rows predating those guards.

Unexposed service requires fresh password/MFA, rechecks password and atomically binds proof at commit. After successful commit only the application's caches, sockets and voice are invalidated/disconnected; the human owner's session survives. Missing runtime dependencies fail closed.
checks: Repository tests passed with FK enforcement on/off, twelve contenders with one retirement winner, rollback restoring tokens, preserved channel/DM history/attachment references, cleanup queue and owner-deletion unblocking.
Wrong owner, human target, platform-admin override, administrator bot, revoked/stale session, disabled/banned owner and bot-owned resource rejection tests passed.
Token insert/update guards and legacy-row validation tests passed, including explicit proof that lookup rejects corrupt rows without depending on the insert trigger.
Focused service tests passed for password/MFA, recovery replay, factor change after proof, failed writes without runtime effects, and bot-only disconnect/cache invalidation.
Full Go test ./... -json passed after the final service and token-guard additions. Existing symlink and external-media smoke test skips remain unverified, not accepted.
Targeted git diff --check passed; existing Windows line-ending warnings only.

migration.compatibility: Additive triggers only; existing bot token rows are not rewritten. No local acceptance or production database was upgraded this turn.
migration.data: An explicitly retired identity is irreversible through the application. A production backup/restore rehearsal is still required; listing rollback statements is not verification.

remaining: Close bot gateway authentication/registration races, persistently validate active connections and prove real token/socket revocation before exposing retirement.
Wire repositories/services, owner/account/application-bound HTTP route, typed consent and real client form; broadcast membership/author updates as appropriate.

Application ownership transfer needs a recipient-accepted handoff and token rotation, not unsolicited assignment of another user's deletion blocker. No transfer implementation or acceptance is claimed here.
Actual browser/independent-client/Windows acceptance, distributed behavior and all remaining P0-P11/release gates remain active.
release: Only source and disposable automated-test databases changed. No real application was removed, no new retirement endpoint was registered, no production deployment/commit/push/merge/Windows update occurred.
